title: Temple of Hercules Victor
source: Two ordinary photographs and reused pinned temple_of_portunus standard PMTiles/Mapzen data.
axis: +X east;+Y up;+Z south. The doorway and stepped access face east.

The open east sector of the mapped cella and stair projection resolve the entrance facing east, independently of the circle bounding-box axis. reconstruction.scope: Temple of Hercules Victor present-day medium-fi exterior: nineteen individually mapped fluted Corinthian shafts and the isolated surviving twentieth base, low circular stepped podium and east entrance steps, round brick/marble cella with a closed recessed arched door, broad shallow tiled conical roof with visible timber underside and small summit cap. Include simplified capital leaf/corner silhouettes and selected protective shaft bands. No lost ancient entablature or original roof is reconstructed. Neighboring Portunus, churches, modern streets and gardens stay independent.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Standard-map parts give podium0.8m, nineteen shaft tops8m, cella8.5m, roof8–10m and cap10.5m above the lower datum. The model follows this approximate envelope: fluted shaft1.0–7.0m, Corinthian crown7.0–8.0m, timber support8.0–8.25m and shallow roof8.25–10.15m. Ordinary frontal and capital pictures guide the present roof, leaf masses, flute/drum/band treatment, brick upper cella and pale lower panels. Exact carvings, repairs, tie bands, door joinery and surveyed heights are not claimed.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Reused pinned temple_of_portunus standard Rome PMTiles/Mapzen extract. The lower datum clears the actual standard-grid triangles beneath each mapped entrance tread and podium, using retained footprint intersections. Foundations extend below the minimum local grade. Native ground and water stay unchanged with no cutout. Exact archaeological floor and modern fence/garden levels remain approximate.
